newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MIM plans A$300 mln Caribbean gold tender.
newsitem.headline: MIM plans A$300 mln Caribbean gold tender.

text.p: Base metals miner MIM Holdings Ltd said on Monday it was planning to tender for a A$300 million gold mining project in the Dominican Republic as part of an ongoing search for new international projects.

MIM general manager, public affairs, Collin Myers told Reuters the company was looking with interest at the Pueblo Viejo project, estimated to contain about 30 million ounces of gold. "This is one of several interests we are considering, Myers said.
"We're taking an interest in this property. It is a recognised gold project in the Dominican Republic," he said.
MIM had estimated the project price and further capital expenditure needed to develop the project would be about A$300 million.
Myers said MIM's search for new projects was part of the group's strategy of focusing on copper and gold as well as copper/gold deposits.
Tendering for the Pueblo Vieja project was due by the middle of the year with the Dominican Republic government expected to decide by the end of 1997.
MIM announced earlier the group was also exploring for gold in Australia, the western states of America, Mexico and Panama.
Myers said two other feasibility studies were proceeding with a study on the A$30 million Sarsfield gold project in north Queensland expected to be completed this year.
MIM's feasibility study on its A$250 million George Fisher lead-zinc project near Mt Isa in north-west Queensland was not expected to be completed until early next year, Myers said.
